front.title: OAuth 2.0 over the Agent Transfer Protocol

abstract.t: This document specifies how the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework is carried over the Agent Transfer Protocol (AGTP). OAuth defines its endpoints as HTTP resources and authenticates clients with secrets or signed assertions. AGTP is a transfer protocol for agent traffic in which every request carries the sending agent's identifier and a proof that the sender holds that agent's key. This document defines an authorization server reachable as an AGTP agent, maps the token, pushed authorization, device authorization, revocation, introspection, and metadata endpoints onto AGTP methods and paths, replaces client authentication with the AGTP request signature, and defines access tokens bound to an Agent-ID. It states which parts of OAuth move to AGTP and which remain on HTTPS. It changes no OAuth grant.
